description: PR455 int8 online embedding quantization (VLLM_EXL3_EMBED_ONLINE_BITS=8) vs strength-zero control (int6, VLLM_EXL3_EMBED_ONLINE_BITS=6). Same strength-zero R30 checkpoint (layer-55 k_proj K6), same 512 v5 shard0 contexts, same R31 replay gate, same BF16 reference and shared head.

method.capture: fidelity.py capture, post-final-norm hook via collective_rpc (VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=1)
method.replay: fidelity_gate.py replay, full-vocabulary KL(BF16||candidate), shared BF16 lm_head, 512 contexts x 2047 positions = 1,048,064 scored positions
method.cluster_bootstrap: source-cluster percentile bootstrap, 330 clusters, 10000 resamples, seed 1

pr455_files_mounted.qwen3_5.py: constructor wiring: quant_config=self.quant_config passed to VocabParallelEmbedding
pr455_files_mounted.qwen3_5_mtp.py: same constructor wiring for MTP draft embedding
pr455_files_mounted.llm_base_proposer.py: embedding sharing compatibility checks for quantized representations

exl3_py: vllm-exl3-multiprecision.py (production multiprecision patch with Exl3OnlineEmbeddingMethod supporting int8 and int6)

Δ0.00 is a measurement timing bug. del layer.weight + del w removes Python references but torch.cuda.memory_allocated() runs before CPython GC collects the freed Parameter. conclusion: int8 embeddings beat int6 on every KLD metric with non-overlapping CI95. The 0.29 GiB VRAM cost buys 22% lower mean KLD. Switching production from VLLM_EXL3_EMBED_ONLINE_BITS=6 to =8 is a fidelity/context tradeoff: ~2k fewer context tokens for 0.000743 lower mean KLD.
